clinician.final_diagnosis: FGD was diagnosed based on isolated glucocorticoid deficiency, hyperpigmentation, and tall stature.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-month-old boy presented with generalized hyperpigmentation and overgrowth since birth. Physical examination confirmed significant overgrowth (length and weight above +3 SD) and hyperpigmentation involving oral mucosa, palms, and soles. Initial investigations revealed very low serum cortisol and very high ACTH, with normal serum aldosterone, indicating isolated glucocorticoid deficiency. An ACTH stimulation test further confirmed severe glucocorticoid deficiency with no cortisol response. Routine labs and brain MRI were normal, ruling out other significant issues. Five months after initiating treatment, the patient showed less pigmentation and a slowing of growth.

ACTH stimulation test showed markedly reduced basal cortisol and no cortisol response, confirming severe glucocorticoid deficiency.
Clinical improvement with less pigmentation and slowing of growth 5 months after initiating treatment.
